difficulty.notes: Classic BigInt RSA.min.js. Unlike case5, there is NO app-level rsa() wrapper: the login code calls encryptedString(key_to_encode, password) directly with a global key. So encryptedString (the RSA primitive) is the anchor here, whereas in case5 it is a 0.5 primitive below rsa(). The role here is relative to each case's call chain. Two near-identical login submit call sites (lines 239/379) are not listed (ambiguous, deep in large handlers); they score 0 as call-site handlers.

task_contract.anchor_definition: encryptedString — the RSA string-encryption function; here it is the shallowest value constructor (no app-level key-binding wrapper exists).

behavior_category.subtype: RSA (BigInt impl) of password called directly with a global key
behavior_category.recompute_check: legacy RSA padding behavior not asserted; static localization only

near_categories.why_not: Only the scalar password is encrypted, not the whole request body.
The token is RSA of user input, not a device/browser digest.

evidence: The RSA encrypt is one function among dozens of BigInt math helpers in a single minified line; no app-level wrapper marks it as the password encryptor.
encryptedString vs decryptedString vs RSAKeyPair vs biMultiply/biAdd... are easy to confuse; two near-identical login call sites.

provenance.label_points_to: a login submit call site (~line 369) that calls encryptedString; the anchor is encryptedString itself
